title: Choose the visual world
question: The homepage needs a new world, and a hero that names the whole operations layer rather than a Xero pipe. The roll assigned Engineering Title Block. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Engineering Title Block
options.lineage: AS and ISO drawing sheets, revision clouds, issue stamps
options.thesis: The homepage is a working drawing of the whole operations set, issued for a yard visit.
options.viewport: A full drawing sheet: the title names jobs, costing, plant, variations, certificates, and ute capture; the title block holds the adapted D1 lockup and Book a yard visit as the issue sign-off.
options.risk: Reads as fabrication-only, or as a poster of a drawing rather than a site the owner can act on.

raised.raise: The field-to-ledger day is a timed cycle: capture, job cost, and the Xero draft are visible before the next beat, not a feature list.
Ops layers register in print order; the ledger is the last keyblock; the mylar ground catches light instead of sitting as a dead fill.
Construction seams stay visible: this is custom-built for the yard, not a shelf product with a skin.

options.label: NCR Job Card
options.lineage: triplicate docket books and numbered job cards
options.thesis: The whole operations layer lives on one numbered job card the yard already knows how to fill.
options.viewport: A landscape job card filling the first screen: job no, costing, plant, variations, certificates, and a photo-capture stub; Book a yard visit is the issue line at the foot.
options.risk: This is also where most trade-ops sites land: paper nostalgia that can look like a form, not a catch.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six luminous gauges, one each for jobs, costing, plant, variations, certificates, and capture; the sweep is the offer.
options.viewport: Two rows of three gauges named for the ops layer; the placard under them is Book a yard visit; Xero is the ground, not a seventh gauge.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the six-pack is the whole layer at a glance. Loses identification: a cockpit is aviation, and it sits one dark dashboard from the SaaS ops look this buyer would throw out.
options.risk: Reads as Linear for tradies in a flight-sim skin.

options.label: Painted Film Poster
options.thesis: One billing-size line names the whole operations set; vignettes around the D1 lockup are jobs, plant, capture, and the ledger.
options.viewport: A landscape hoarding: giant adapted D1 as the portrait, title in outlined yellow, four vignettes for field, job brain, certificates, and Xero; Book a yard visit is the billing.
options.case: Holds clarity: scale makes the catch unmissable and the montage proves more than dockets. Loses identification: South West trade owners do not live in film-poster grammar.
options.risk: Reads as the parent site's irreverent high-end voice, which this sector will not buy.

options.label: Crank Paper Menagerie
options.thesis: Turn the crank and the day processes: ute, docket, job cost, draft invoice — the mechanism is the pitch.
options.viewport: A landscape stage with a crank at the base; four paper figures in procession; Book a yard visit is the caption strip.
options.case: Holds clarity: you see the field-to-ledger loop. Loses identification: paper toys read pretty, which this buyer already rejects.
options.risk: Looks like a craft project, not a yard visit.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.thesis: The field-to-ledger loop as live source: each layer is a pattern, edits land on the next cycle.
options.viewport: A stage-scale code buffer whose layers are jobs, capture, costing, and Xero; Book a yard visit is the line about to evaluate.
options.case: Fuses poorly: live code is software theatre, and the owner does not identify with a rave floor.
options.kept: Edits apply on the next cycle; upcoming changes are visible before they land.
options.risk: Looks like a developer toy, which is the miss this buyer named.

options.label: Đông Hồ Shell Ground
options.thesis: Ops layers print colour by colour onto a ground that catches light; the ledger is the last keyblock.
options.viewport: A centred print of the yard with colour blocks for jobs, capture, and certificates; Xero prints last; Book a yard visit sits in the character block.
options.case: Fuses poorly: folk print is not this yard's graphic home, and a centred subject hides the ops layer.
options.kept: Colour layers register in order; the keyblock prints last; the ground catches light.
options.risk: Reads as a gallery object, not an operations offer.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: The custom system is built in visible courses, each thumb-smoothed seam a layer of the yard's ops.
options.viewport: A vertical tower of courses labelled jobs, costing, plant, variations, certificates, capture; Book a yard visit is the course being laid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: earth coils speak to civil dirt, not sparkies or fleet, and slow construction does not name the offer.
options.kept: Visible courses and seams: you can see how a custom system was made.
options.risk: Looks like a ceramics studio, not a South West yard.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What SimPRO, Tradify, and AroFlo already look like, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A dark SaaS hero, a job-app screenshot, three feature columns, and Book a yard visit in the header.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
